surfaces.part: lion-head spout pillar with cap and water jet

answer.evidence: The silhouette width grows from 30 at row 15 to 60 at rows 24-37 and then narrows to 18 by row 47. This is an elliptical basin. Teal water (rows 18-36) is visible inside the opening, with a dark eave shadow at row 21 under the back rim. Rim stones span rows 15-37, and a light front-edge line sits at rows 37-38. Below it is a grey stone front face of about 10 rows (38-47) with vertical joints. The lion-head pillar, its cap, and the water jet stand on or over the basin, so they are decor. The basin is the main body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate fountain reads clearly, but its measured facts match the shallow look. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line rather than a tinted material tone. Near-flat coverage is 32%, against 0-13% for the detailed references (hedge 0%, stall 13%, well 0%). It has 8 visible tones per tile, versus 17-20 for the stall and well, which are the closest props in size and complexity. By eye, the stone basin and the pedestal are mostly smooth grey with 2-3 steps and no per-stone shading, no mortar or speckle and little moss or wear. The water has only a few flat blue bands and no ripple dots. The lion head is small and simple. Beside the roofed well, which has shaded stones and a textured roof, the fountain looks flatter and more sticker-like.
